name: Idiopathic Dropped Head Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Idiopathic Dropped Head Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Progressive severe weakness of neck extensor muscles causing chin-on-chest deformity
No evidence of generalized neuromuscular disorders such as myasthenia gravis or motor neuron disease
EMG showing myopathic changes localized to cervical paraspinal muscles
MRI or muscle biopsy demonstrating isolated neck extensor myopathy without inflammatory or neurogenic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive dropped head posture due to neck extensor weakness with exclusion of systemic neuromuscular diseases
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by EMG and imaging; muscle biopsy may be required to exclude inflammatory myopathies

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe neck extensor muscle weakness causing chin-on-chest deformity
searchTerms: weak neck muscles causing chin drop
head bent forward due to muscle weakness

pathognomonic.symptomName: Inability to maintain upright head posture

common.symptomName: Neck pain localized to cervical paraspinal region
Fatigability of neck muscles on sustained posture
Difficulty swallowing due to head position
searchTerms: difficulty eating due to neck posture
swallowing problems related to head tilt
speech difficulty caused by neck position
impaired talking due to head tilt
slight sensory changes in upper limbs

occasional.symptomName: Mild respiratory compromise due to posture
searchTerms: mild respiratory difficulty due to neck position

rare.symptomName: Dysphagia due to pharyngeal muscle involvement
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing from throat muscle weakness
swallowing problems due to muscle involvement

rare.symptomName: Upper motor neuron signs in cervical region
searchTerms: signs of nerve damage in neck
upper motor neuron symptoms in cervical spine
spasticity and reflex changes in neck area

laboratory: Creatine kinase mildly elevated or normal
imaging: MRI cervical spine showing selective neck extensor muscle atrophy
Muscle biopsy showing nonspecific myopathic changes without inflammation
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; idiopathic etiology
other: Electromyography showing myopathic pattern localized to neck extensors

distinguishingFeatures: Fluctuating weakness including ocular and bulbar muscles
Presence of upper and lower motor neuron signs
Systemic symptoms such as rash or interstitial lung disease

redFlags: Rapidly progressive neck weakness with systemic symptoms
Presence of upper motor neuron signs
Bulbar muscle involvement causing respiratory compromise
references: Katz JS, Wolfe GI. Dropped head syndrome. Neurol Clin. 2005;23(3):717-728.
Katz JS, Barohn RJ. Isolated neck extensor myopathy: a common cause of dropped head syndrome. Neurology. 1996;46(3):917-920.
